item.title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.

item.title: Life in the Rohingya camps in Bangladesh is becoming more precarious.
Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya
item.description:
The highest United Nations court ruled on Thursday that thousands of killings and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces against the Rohingya Muslim minority population in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.

The decision, seven years after the case was filed by predominantly Muslim Gambia, marked only the fourth time since the Nazi Holocaust that an international court ruled that the legal threshold to prove genocide had been met.

It was the first time the court held a state responsible for genocide.

“The court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence as well as acts of extreme violence against children and attacked fleeing Rohingya,” presiding Judge Yuji Iwasawa said in a reading of the decision.

The panel found “that the Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in Northern Rakhine State.”

Myanmar’s government did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment.

Decision is expected to influence other genocide cases

Judges found that Myanmar’s military carried out mass executions of men and boys, committed widespread rape and sexual violence against Rohingya women and burned or razed hundreds of villages during so-called clearance operations.

The military actively spread hate speech targeting the Rohingya population, they said. The court’s ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

Genocide has rarely been established in international courts, largely because prosecutors must prove a specific intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial or religious group.

The decision by the International Court of Justice, or World Court, is expected to have repercussions far beyond Myanmar, including for South Africa’s 2023 case accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza.

The first major decision by the court in more than a decade on the application of the 1948 Genocide Convention will be pored over by legal experts for clues to how the bench assessed state responsibility in the alleged commission of international crimes.

Both Israel and Myanmar deny genocide and say their forces responded legitimately to attacks by armed groups.

In a major legal victory for Gambia, the court found the state responsible for genocide resulting from a military offensive that drove at least 700,000 Muslim Rohingya from Buddhist-majority Myanmar.

A panel of 15 judges said “the only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar’s actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part of the protected group namely the Rohingya population in Northern Rakhine state,” meeting the legal threshold for genocide.

The court said Myanmar had an obligation to compensate the Rohingya for the violations it had committed, to be determined at a later date.

Myanmar must also allow the “safe and dignified return to their place of residence and the reunification of families for the Rohingya displaced as a result of Myanmar’s wrongful acts,” it said.

International courts previously only recognised genocide during the 1994 Rwanda genocide, the 1995 Srebrenica killings in Bosnia, and atrocities by Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge in the late 1970s.

While rulings by the ICJ, which settles disputes between states and rules on alleged breaches of international treaties, are final, the court has very limited options to enforce them.

It is distinct from the International Criminal Court, which prosecutes individuals for war crimes, crimes against ​humanity and genocide and can impose jail terms.

item.title: Parts of Bangladesh shut down in protests by Hasina's party, ex-leader Yunus's home set ablaze
item.description:
Parts of Bangladesh shut down as police said two ruling party members were killed and the ancestral home of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in violence ahead of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return planned for December.

Hasina’s Awami League party called Thursday’s nationwide lockdown in culmination of a week-long campaign of protests and rallies against the government’s rejection of her request for a new passport and identity card that would allow her return.

To deter violence, 97 platoons of the Bangladesh Border Guard have fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur, considered to have many Hasina supporters, its spokesperson, Shariful Islam, said.

Police said former interim leader Yunus’ ancestral home in Chattogram, about 300 km southeast of Dhaka, the capital, was set on fire late on Wednesday.

It is likely that flammable substances were thrown into an unused ground-floor room, Mozammel Haque, chief of the area’s Panchlaish police station, told Reuters, but Yunus’ paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, are safe.

Reuters could not immediately reach the Yunus Centre think tank that speaks on his behalf to seek comment.

Yunus and his government, which led Bangladesh after Hasina’s ouster, have faced hostility from her supporters.

More violence

During the last 10 days of protests, police have reported dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles being set afire in at least 28 districts, injuring several police officials and members of the public, media have said.

Tuesday marks a year since Hasina was sentenced to death by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising against her in 2024.

She has lived in exile in neighbouring India after fleeing Dhaka following violent protests demanding her resignation in August 2024.

On Thursday, authorities detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, who faces charges over several killings during the 2024 protests, from his house in Dhaka, police officer Mohammad Khalid Mansur told Reuters.

At least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires since Nov 10, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday, the bank said.

On Tuesday, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused Awami League leaders abroad of inciting supporters to destabilise Bangladesh and torch property, adding that those involved in violence would be identified and prosecuted.

Awami League leaders, most of them in hiding, could not be reached for comment.

item.description:
The High Court has suspended admission tests at all public universities across the country, including Dhaka University, until 31 December.

A High Court bench comprising Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice SM Ifthekhar Uddin Mahmud issued the order, along with a rule, today, Wednesday, following the preliminary hearing of a writ petition.

Dhaka University rejects UGC’s call, keeps admission tests on schedule

Supreme Court lawyer Kamrun Nahar Mahmud filed the writ petition last Thursday. She herself presented arguments in support of the petition before the court.

Later, lawyer Kamrun Nahar Mahmud told Prothom Alo that the High Court has suspended admission tests at all public universities in the country, including the University of Dhaka, until 31 December.

item.title: Govt to rebuild Bangladesh as fascism-free dignified state: PM
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today, Saturday, said his government is committed to rebuilding a fascism-free Bangladesh as a dignified and exemplary state on the world stage, pledging continued respect and support for freedom fighters and their families.

"The government's pledge is to place the independent Bangladesh, which the valiant freedom fighters courageously established for us, in a position of dignity," he said, adding that the state would continue to extend respect and support to the freedom fighters and their families to the best of its capacity and resources.

The Prime Minister was addressing a reception for gallantry award-winning freedom fighters of the Armed Forces and their heirs on the occasion of Armed Forces Day-2026. The reception was held this morning at the Army Multipurpose Complex in Dhaka Cantonment.

Noting that freedom fighters were conferred gallantry titles such as Bir Sreshtha, Bir Uttam, Bir Bikram and Bir Protik for their heroic role in the Liberation War, the Prime Minister said more important than any title is the glory of fighting for and winning a nation's independence.

"Not everyone gets the opportunity to achieve such glory in a lifetime. That is why the freedom fighters are unique and extraordinary," he said.

Addressing the freedom fighters and family members present, he said some of them had the good fortune to take part directly in the Liberation War, while others lost family members as martyrs. "All of you share that glory, directly or indirectly. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to you," he said.

Recalling the sacrifices of 1971, the Prime Minister said independent Bangladesh was established at the cost of the lives of millions, the honour of countless mothers and sisters, and the sacrifices of those who were wounded and crippled.

He paid deep respect to all martyrs of the Liberation War, expressed profound sympathy and condolences to the wounded freedom fighters and the families of martyrs, and prayed for the salvation of the departed souls.

Describing felicitation of the freedom fighters as a responsibility of the state, he said the honour and reception accorded to them on the historic Armed Forces Day reflect the state's obligation to them. "By honouring them, the state has tried, at least to some extent, to discharge that obligation," he said.

Identifying himself as the son of a freedom fighter, Tarique Rahman said he was proud to attend the programme, and that any glory or success of the Liberation War and the freedom fighters moves him deeply. He said Major Ziaur Rahman, the proclaimer of Bangladesh's independence, was himself a proud member of the armed forces, which was also a matter of pride for the force.

The Prime Minister said that every time the BNP has been given the responsibility of running the state by the people's mandate, it has taken various positive steps for the Liberation War and the welfare of freedom fighters.

He said the late former prime minister Khaleda Zia established the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs in 2001 to uphold the glory of the Liberation War and ensure the welfare of freedom fighters, a decision that later proved timely. The Jatiya Muktijoddha Council Act was enacted in 2002, he added.

Highlighting the freedom fighters' contribution, he said many of them are now weary with age, but the glow of independence still shines in their eyes in the twilight of their lives.

He thanked all concerned for the commendable initiative the Armed Forces Division takes every year to formally honour these 'living legends' scattered across the country.

The Prime Minister concluded his speech by paying deep respect once again to the martyrs of the Liberation War.

Earlier, the premier paid homage to the martyred members of the Armed Forces by placing a wreath at the altar of Shikha Anirban in Dhaka Cantonment. After laying the wreath, he stood in solemn silence for a while as a mark of profound respect for the martyrs.

A contingent of the Army, Navy and Air Force presented a guard of honour while the bugle sounded the last post. The prime minister later signed the visitors' book kept at the memorial.

On arrival at Shikha Anirban, the Prime Minister was received by his Defence Adviser Brigadier General (Retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam, Army Chief General Waqar-Uz-Zaman, Navy Chief Admiral Khondkar Misbah Ul Azim, Air Chief Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan and Principal Staff Officer of the Armed Forces Division Lieutenant General Mir Mushfiqur Rahman.

item.title: Bangladesh up three notches in UN e-govt index
item.description:
Bangladesh has moved up three places to rank 97th among 194 countries in the United Nations E-Government Development Index (EGDI) 2026, entering the double-digit bracket for the first time.

The country was ranked 100th in the previous edition in 2024. It scored 0.6893 this year, its highest ever, and remains in the "High EGDI" group.

Bangladesh also recorded its all-time highest scores in two of the index's components. Its Online Service Index (OSI) score stood at 0.81, while its Telecommunication Infrastructure Index (TII) score was 0.69, according to release of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology.

The results come from the 2026 UN E-Government Survey, which put the Republic of Korea at the top of the digital government ranking. The survey is a biennial publication prepared by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA).

The EGDI is a composite measure of a country's readiness, capacity and progress in using e-government to deliver public services. It is a weighted average of normalised scores on three dimensions: the Online Service Index, the Telecommunications Infrastructure Index and the Human Capital Index.

The global average EGDI rose 4.6 per cent, from 0.6382 in 2024 to 0.6675 in 2026. Bangladesh's score of 0.6893 is above the 2026 global average.

Of the 194 countries assessed, 151 now fall in the high or very high EGDI groups, up from 138 in 2024.

item.title: ত্রিপক্ষীয় বৈঠকে ট্রাম্প, শি ও পুতিন
‘জেনোসাইডের লক্ষ্য’ নিয়ে রোহিঙ্গা নিপীড়নে মিয়ানমারকে দোষী সাব্যস্ত করলেন আইসিজে
item.description:
২০১৭ সালে রোহিঙ্গাদের ওপর চালানো দমন–পীড়নের ঘটনায় মিয়ানমারকে ‘গোষ্ঠী নিধনের (জেনোসাইড) লক্ষ্য’ নিয়ে নির্বিচার মানুষ হত্যার অভিযোগে দোষী সাব্যস্ত করেছেন জাতিসংঘের সর্বোচ্চ আদালত। সাত বছর ধরে বিচারকাজ শেষে আন্তর্জাতিক বিচার আদালত (আইসিজে) আজ বৃহস্পতিবার ঘোষিত রায়ে এ কথা বলেছেন।

নেদারল্যান্ডসের দ্য হেগ শহরে অবস্থিত এ আদালতের সভাপতি বিচারক ইয়াসাওয়া ইয়ুজি বলেছেন, ২০১৭ সালের তথাকথিত ক্লিয়ারেন্স অপারেশনে মিয়ানমারের নিরাপত্তা বাহিনী প্রায় ১০ হাজার রোহিঙ্গাকে হত্যা করেছে। তারা ব্যাপক যৌন সহিংসতা চালিয়েছে, শিশুদের ওপর চরম সহিংসতা করেছে এবং বিপুলসংখ্যক রোহিঙ্গা বাংলাদেশে পালিয়ে যাওয়ার চেষ্টা করার সময় তাদের ওপর হামলা চালিয়েছে।

জেনোসাইডের লক্ষ্য নিয়ে মিয়ানমারের নিরাপত্তা বাহিনী যে এসব কাজ করেছে, এমন সিদ্ধান্তে পৌঁছানোর যৌক্তিক ভিত্তি রয়েছে বলে উল্লেখ করেছেন ইওয়াসাওয়া ইয়ুজি। তিনি বলেন, ২০১৭ সালে ওই অভিযান ঘিরে যে পরিস্থিতি তৈরি করা হয়েছিল, তা মিয়ানমারের নিরাপত্তা বাহিনীর চালানো সহিংসতার অনুকূল পরিবেশ সৃষ্টি করেছিল। একই সঙ্গে রোহিঙ্গা জনগোষ্ঠীর একটি অংশকে ধ্বংস করার বিষয়ে মিয়ানমারের অভিপ্রায় গড়ে ওঠার ভিত্তিও তৈরি করেছিল।

আন্তর্জাতিক বিচার আদালতের এই বিচারক বলেন, আদালতের কাছে উপস্থাপিত সব প্রমাণ একসঙ্গে বিবেচনায় নিলে এ সিদ্ধান্তে পৌঁছানোর যৌক্তিক ভিত্তি পাওয়া যায় যে মিয়ানমারের নিরাপত্তা বাহিনী জেনোসাইডের লক্ষ্য নিয়ে কাজ করেছে।

২০১৭ সালের আগস্টে বাংলাদেশ সীমান্তবর্তী আরাকান রাজ্যে রোহিঙ্গা মুসলিমদের ওপর ব্যাপক দমন অভিযান চালায় মিয়ানমারের সেনাবাহিনী। তাদের নিষ্ঠুরতার মুখে ঘরবাড়ি ছেড়ে বাংলাদেশে এসে আশ্রয় নেয় সাত লাখের বেশি রোহিঙ্গা। এখনো তারা বাংলাদেশের কক্সবাজার ও নোয়াখালীর ভাসান চরে শরণার্থীশিবিরে আশ্রয় নিয়ে আছে।

রোহিঙ্গাদের ওপর চালানো এ হত্যাকাণ্ডের ঘটনায় ১৯৪৮ সালের জাতিসংঘের জেনোসাইড সনদ লঙ্ঘনের অভিযোগে ২০১৯ সালে আইসিজেতে মামলা করেছিল গাম্বিয়া। সাত বছর ধরে বিচারকাজ পরিচালনার পর আজ রায় ঘোষণা করলেন আইসিজের বিচারকেরা।

item.description:
মিয়ানমারে রোহিঙ্গা মুসলিম ও অন্যান্য সংখ্যালঘু জনগোষ্ঠীর মানবাধিকার পরিস্থিতি নিয়ে জাতিসংঘ সাধারণ পরিষদে ইসলামী সহযোগিতা সংস্থা (ওআইসি) ও ইউরোপীয় ইউনিয়নের (ইইউ) উত্থাপিত একটি প্রস্তাব বিপুল ভোটে গৃহীত হয়েছে।
বুধবার অনুষ্ঠিত ভোটাভুটিতে প্রস্তাবটির পক্ষে ১২৮টি দেশ ভোট দেয়। বিপক্ষে ভোট দেয় ৬টি দেশ এবং ভোটদানে বিরত থাকে ৩৩টি দেশ। আজ ঢাকায় প্রাপ্ত এক তথ্য বিবরণীতে এসব তথ্য জানানো হয়। প্রস্তাবটি গৃহীত হওয়ার আগে বাংলাদেশের পক্ষে বক্তব্যে জাতিসংঘে বাংলাদেশের চার্জ দ্য অ্যাফেয়ার্স রাষ্ট্রদূত সঞ্চিতা হক দীর্ঘদিনের রোহিঙ্গা সংকট সমাধানে জরুরি পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণের ওপর গুরুত্বারোপ করেন।
তিনি বলেন, রোহিঙ্গাদের ব্যাপকভাবে বাস্তুচ্যুত হওয়ার নয় বছর অতিবাহিত হলেও তাদের প্রত্যাবাসনে কোনও অর্থবহ অগ্রগতি অর্জিত হয়নি, বরং দীর্ঘায়িত এ বাস্তুচ্যুতির কারণে বাংলাদেশ ও আশ্রয়দাতা স্থানীয় জনগোষ্ঠীকে নানামুখী সামাজিক, অর্থনৈতিক, পরিবেশগত ও নিরাপত্তাজনিত চ্যালেঞ্জ মোকাবিলা করতে হচ্ছে।
রাষ্ট্রদূত সঞ্চিতা হক গাম্বিয়া বনাম মিয়ানমার মামলায় আন্তর্জাতিক বিচার আদালতের (আইসিজে) আসন্ন রায়ের গুরুত্বও তুলে ধরেন। তিনি বলেন, এ রায় রোহিঙ্গাদের ন্যায়বিচার প্রতিষ্ঠা ও দায়বদ্ধতা নিশ্চিত করার ক্ষেত্রে একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ মাইলফলক হয়ে উঠবে বলে আশা করা হচ্ছে।
এ বছরের প্রস্তাবে মিয়ানমারের সামরিক বাহিনী ও আরাকান আর্মির হাতে রোহিঙ্গাদের ওপর সংঘটিত গুরুতর মানবাধিকার লঙ্ঘন ও নির্যাতনের বিষয়টি তুলে ধরা হয়েছে। এতে অবিলম্বে সহিংসতা বন্ধ, মানবিক সহায়তা নিশ্চিত এবং ন্যায়বিচার ও জবাবদিহিতা প্রতিষ্ঠার আহ্বান জানানো হয়েছে।
পাশাপাশি, ২০২৬ সালের জয়েন্ট রেসপন্স প্ল্যানসহ রোহিঙ্গাদের জন্য মানবিক সহায়তায় পর্যাপ্ত অর্থায়ন নিশ্চিত করা, তাদের রাজনৈতিক ও ভোটাধিকার পুনঃপ্রতিষ্ঠা এবং স্বেচ্ছায়, নিরাপদ, মর্যাদাপূর্ণ ও টেকসই প্রত্যাবাসন ও পুনর্বাসনের অনুকূল পরিবেশ তৈরির ওপর গুরুত্বারোপ করা হয়েছে।
প্রস্তাবটি বাস্তবায়নে আন্তর্জাতিক সম্প্রদায় ও আঞ্চলিক অংশীজনদের সম্মিলিত প্রচেষ্টা জোরদারের আহ্বান জানান রাষ্ট্রদূত সঞ্চিতা হক। তিনি স্পষ্টভাবে বলেন, রোহিঙ্গা সংকটের সৃষ্টি হয়েছে মিয়ানমারে, তাই এর স্থায়ী সমাধানও খুঁজে বের করতে হবে মিয়ানমারেই।
প্রস্তাবে আন্তর্জাতিক অপরাধ আদালতের (আইসিসি) প্রসঙ্গ অন্তর্ভুক্ত থাকায় যুক্তরাষ্ট্র এ ব্যাপারে ভোটাভুটির আহ্বান জানায়। ভোটের ব্যাখ্যায় দেশটি জানায়, বিভিন্ন প্রস্তাবে আইসিসির উল্লেখের বিষয়ে তাদের একটি সাধারণ বিরোধিতার অবস্থান রয়েছে। তবে মিয়ানমারে মানবাধিকার লঙ্ঘনের বিষয়ে যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের অবস্থান অপরিবর্তিত রয়েছে বলে স্পষ্ট করে দেশটি।
একই সঙ্গে এক দশকেরও বেশি সময় ধরে ১২ লাখের অধিক রোহিঙ্গাকে আশ্রয় দিয়ে বাংলাদেশের উদারতা ও মানবিক ভূমিকার ভূয়সী প্রশংসা করে যুক্তরাষ্ট্র।

item.title: Mideast crisis ‘largest threat’ to energy security ever: IEA
item.description:
IRAN-CRISIS/INSURANCE-SHIPPING

The crisis in the Middle East sparked in February by the US and Israeli bombing of Iran has created the “largest threat” to energy security in history, the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned Thursday.

The agency said in its flagship annual World Energy Outlook that consumers were increasingly footing the bill as the world runs out of ways to absorb the impact of the conflict on energy supplies.

The crisis, just like previous energy shocks, would certainly leave “lasting marks”, the agency warned.

Gulf countries have been struggling to export oil since Iran began blockading the Strait of Hormuz and targeting tankers in the area, following US and Israeli strikes that sparked the crisis in February.

Despite attempts by the United States to escort vessels through the channel -- which pre-crisis carried about one-fifth of global oil shipments -- supply lines remain severely disrupted.

“The Strait of Hormuz crisis has created the largest threat to energy security in history, one that dwarfs the scale of the oil shocks of the 1970s,” IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in his foreword to the report.

He highlighted the efforts countries had taken to protect households, with producing nations bringing more supplies into the market and using alternative routes, and China buying less from international markets.

“Governments have intervened to try and provide some shelter for consumers, but they have nonetheless faced higher prices and, in some cases, shortfalls of supply,” Birol wrote.

The report said elsewhere that “increasingly it is falling to consumers -- and high prices -- to absorb the impact as other buffers are run down”.

Birol had struck a more hopeful tone in July when he wrote that the oil market was still benefiting from “several cushioning factors”.

‘No pathway’ back

 The IEA’s report comes as nations meet for the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, with governments under pressure to tackle climate change after a year of searing heatwaves and wildfires in Europe, and deadly floods in Nepal.

The agency uses three scenarios for its energy outlook: a cautious one takes into account policies that are currently in place, a middle scenario looks at “stated” government policies including measures that have yet to be adopted, and a third considers a world that reaches net zero emissions by 2050.

In its middle scenario, the IEA forecasts that global oil demand will reach a peak around 2030 before a slow decline, while gas demand would increase until around 2035.

For this report, it also adds two other scenarios based on what might happen if the Middle East crisis persists.

“While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” Birol said in a press release.

“And I don’t see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before.”

item.title: Humaiun: Dhaka eyes Rohingya repatriation within 18 months
item.description:
Bangladesh will step up talks with the United Nations and bilateral partners to secure safe passage for Rohingyas back to Myanmar within 12 to 18 months, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said.
"We will pursue these discussions vigorously so that we can provide safe passage within a year to a year and a half," he told journalists at a media briefing on the International Court of Justice (ICJ) judgment on Rohingya genocide.
Kobir said the ruling gave Bangladesh a stronger legal basis to press for safe repatriation and compensation for affected communities.
He outlined the timeframe in response to a question on how Bangladesh would accelerate repatriation, saying that any return would depend on putting safeguards in place in Myanmar's Rakhine State so that the Rohingyas could go home safely and rebuild their lives.
The state minister said Bangladesh would work with UN agencies, key regional partners and other stakeholders to establish conditions for safe return.
In his prepared remarks, he described prompt and sustainable repatriation as the only effective solution to the protracted crisis.
Kobir said Bangladesh would also work through the UN system and with its bilateral partners to ensure that compensation is provided to affected Rohingya communities.
Asked whether Dhaka would pursue a bilateral mechanism with Myanmar to determine compensation, he said bilateral efforts alone could not secure the necessary reparations and that the process would require the involvement of several countries and agencies.
He said financial compensation could never make up for the lives lost or the suffering of bereaved families.
Bangladesh would, however, he said, seek to persuade Myanmar to provide compensation and take other measures that would help surviving family members return and rebuild their lives.
Kobir said Bangladesh would work within the UN system to press for follow-up on compensation if The Gambia, a party to the case, brought the matter before the UN Security Council.
Asked whether Bangladesh would formally propose deploying an international peacekeeping force in Rakhine, Kobir said Dhaka would engage a wider range of UN agencies and bilateral partners if the matter came before the council. He gave no commitment to a formal peacekeeping proposal.
He said that the ICJ had found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine State.
The state minister described it as the first judgment in the court's history to find a state responsible for committing genocide.
He said the court recognised the Rohingya as a distinct ethnic group with their own language, culture and identity, and noted that discriminatory laws, restrictions and campaigns of hatred had progressively curtailed their rights over several decades.
Kobir said the court found that Myanmar had failed to prevent genocidal acts by individuals acting alongside its security forces and to preserve evidence as required by its 2020 order on provisional measures.
He said the court directed Myanmar to enact effective legislation to prevent genocide, end ongoing violence and investigate individuals reasonably suspected of involvement in genocide, with prosecution and punishment where appropriate.
The ruling also addressed reparations for victims through restitution and compensation, he added.
Kobir said the judgment was final, could not be appealed and was legally binding on the parties to the case.
Bangladesh, which hosts around 1.3 million forcibly displaced Rohingyas, had closely followed the proceedings although it was not a party to the case, he said.
The state minister thanked the government and people of The Gambia for bringing the case on Nov 11, 2019, as well as the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the 11 countries that filed written declarations before the court.
He also acknowledged the Rohingya community's years of advocacy and the support of host communities in Cox's Bazar.
Kobir urged the international community to act swiftly on the judgment and called on development partners and donors to continue humanitarian assistance for displaced Rohingyas and Bangladeshi host communities until repatriation is complete.
Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury was present at the briefing, among others.

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin summit: What did it achieve?
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, bringing together the leaders of the world’s three most powerful military powers amid heightened geopolitical tensions.
Xi hailed the talks as “groundbreaking,” saying discussions ranged from global governance and denuclearization to the war in Ukraine and energy security.
The “peace declaration” released after their meeting made no mention of Russia’s war in Ukraine or the US-led war in Iran.
Instead, the three leaders agreed to pursue reforms of the United Nations, limit the role of the International Criminal Court and reaffirm their commitment to avoiding nuclear war. They also pledged to boost supplies of refined petroleum products to address global energy challenges.
The tightly choreographed meeting fueled concerns that Beijing, Washington and Moscow could seek to reshape the international order around competing spheres of influence.
While Xi said the talks with Trump and Putin were “positive, constructive and fruitful,” Trump heralded the gathering as “really making history.”
For Putin, the three-way talks, and his meetings with both leaders separately earlier, offered a chance to show the world that he was on par with the leaders of the US and China, despite Western efforts to isolate him since he launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Emma Chanlett-Avery, senior director for Political-Security Affairs at the Asia Society Policy Institute (Aspi), said Putin had the most to gain from the meeting as “he appeared on the world stage as one of the dominant players in the world.”
Chim Lee, a senior analyst with The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU), echoed this view.
The meeting itself is a “major outcome for Russia,” he told DW, pointing to Russian media coverage that has cast it as “reinforcing Russia’s standing in the world.”
The joint statement also said the leaders are committed to work to reduce nuclear risks and prevent nuclear proliferation.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February.
Trump has said he wants “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
But Beijing has so far been reluctant to accept limits as its estimated arsenal of around 500 warheads remains far smaller than those of Russia and the US.
Moscow and Washington are believed to possess more than 5,000 warheads each.
Lee said China is unlikely to participate in a trilateral institutionalized setting to control nuclear arms.
“The gap between China’s nuclear arsenal and those of Russia and US is still quite large. From China’s perspective, it doesn’t seem to make a lot of sense to put the three powers in the same bucket in this area.”
The expert believes Trump attended the meeting as he is “actively thinking about his legacy in the final two years in office.”
“So, in this context, the idea of setting up a trilateral nuclear arms control arrangement would have been a very big achievement,” Lee said.
But, in the end, the declaration said the countries would merely engage in “dialogue” on the issue, avoiding any explicit commitments to downsize their nuclear stockpiles.
China initially hesitated to organize the trilateral summit as it did not want to be explicitly tied to Russia’s war in Ukraine and harm Beijing’s efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability.
The Chinese government, which is working to rebalance economic ties with the EU, was also wary of appearing to form a G3 club with Washington and Moscow, which could alienate other global partners.
Chanlett-Avery said that China had some degree of discomfort in convening this meeting, worried about getting involved in Ukraine issues.
But Beijing eventually “managed to get the outcome they wanted” and kept the European conflict out of the meeting’s focus, she noted.
“China was able to show off Shenzhen and all of its sparkling high-tech features. They convened a successful international meeting that grabbed lots of headlines,” she added. “So, I think China probably came out feeling okay.”
Prior to the summit, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned of a “second Yalta,” referring to the Yalta Conference held in Crimea in 1945.
That meeting saw the Allied powers decide on the post-war European order following the end of World War II.
In Shenzhen, Putin stressed that Russia, the US and China, as victors in World War II and veto-wielding members of the UN Security Council, bore a “joint responsibility for maintaining international peace.”
But Ying-Yu Lin, Associate Professor at Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies at Taiwan’s Tamkang University, said the Yalta comparison “is a bit of a stretch,” given the vast differences between 1945 and now.
Putin also said that all three leaders “agree that it’s a useful format,” and such meetings could take place again.
Lee, the EIU expert, said the trilateral setup “is unlikely to be just a one-off” and there will probably be more such meetings in the coming years.
“Especially from the US side to have this kind of setup, there will be some interest in maintaining warm relations with both China and Russia,” he underlined.

item.title: If united, no one will dare turn Bangladesh into a subservient state: PM
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said no one would ever again dare to turn Bangladesh into a subservient state if patriotic people, a democratic government accountable to the people and the armed forces remained united in the spirit of "Bangladesh First".

“Deep conspiracies were hatched in the past to trample Bangladesh's independence and sovereignty and tarnish the image of the armed forces. But the armed forces have always played an important role in safeguarding the country's independence and protecting the interests of its people,” he said.

The Prime Minister made the remarks this afternoon while addressing a reception at Senakunja in Dhaka Cantonment marking Armed Forces Day 2026.

On arrival at the venue, Army Chief General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Navy Chief Admiral Khondkar Misbah Ul Azim and Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan received the Prime Minister and his wife Zubaida Rahman.

The Prime Minister was then escorted to the stage, where the national anthem was played.

The Prime Minister said the armed forces played a landmark role in favour of the country and its people at every important juncture- the Liberation War of 1971, the soldiers-and-people's revolution of 7 November, 1975, and the anti-fascist mass uprising of 5 August, 2024.

The premier said that just as brave freedom fighters had won independence by laying down their lives in 1971, brave students and people protected the freedom of the country and its people through the bloody mass uprising in 2024.

He said there were two main responsibilities to honour the martyrs. First- to safeguard at any cost the independence and sovereignty won through their sacrifices, and second- to build the safe, self-reliant, democratic welfare state they had dreamt of.

Highlighting the glorious history of the armed forces, the Prime Minister said their journey began with independence and the Liberation War. On 21 November, 1971, the army, navy and air force jointly mounted resistance and counterattacks against the occupation forces on the battlefield. Since then the day has been observed as Armed Forces Day.

Tarique Rahman asks BNP, its 3 affiliated organisations to remain active on the streets

He said Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, the proclaimer of independence, was a proud member of the army. When the brutal attack by the Pakistani occupation forces began on the night of 25 March, 1971, Major Ziaur Rahman, then second-in-command of the 8th East Bengal Regiment in Chattogram, declared "We revolt" and plunged into armed resistance.

Citing Shaheed Ziaur Rahman's own writings, the Prime Minister said he ordered army officers, junior commissioned officers (JCOs) and soldiers to take up arms at 2:15 am on 26 March. The next day, 27 March, he re-broadcast the declaration of independence from Kalurghat Radio Station.

The armed forces of a country are a symbol of its independence, sovereignty, honour, glory, courage and valour, he said, adding that deep conspiracies had been hatched at various times in post-independence Bangladesh to damage the image of the armed forces and undermine the country's sovereignty.

He said soldiers and people had united on 7 November, 1975 to foil an attempt to turn the country into a subservient state. But the conspirators did not stop, he said, adding that army officers were indiscriminately massacred at Pilkhana in 2009 in the name of the BDR mutiny.

Expressing resolve to build a more modern, stronger and technology-driven armed forces, the Prime Minister said that, alongside ensuring the political and economic empowerment of the people to make the state secure and strong, the government has begun implementing plans to enhance the forces' capabilities.

He said that, beyond land security, safeguarding the country's airspace and maritime boundaries was essential for a modern state.

The capabilities of the army, navy and air force, he said, reach their full potential only when they become part of an integrated national defence system. To that end, the government has already prepared new planning guidance.

He said global security strategy was evolving beyond conventional military boundaries into a multidimensional, technology-driven and integrated framework. Building the necessary capabilities in cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, drones, electronic warfare and space-based surveillance was part of the government's plans, he added.

Stressing the importance of discipline in the armed forces, the Prime Minister said maintaining the chain of command, professional integrity and efficiency is essential to strengthen the forces and sustaining public confidence in the institution.

Govt to rebuild Bangladesh as fascism-free dignified state: PM

Noting that the government is also committed to improving the professional skill, training facilities and welfare of armed forces personnel, as well as quality of living of their families, he said, a Joint Services Human Resource Management Board has already been formed to improve human resource management.

Announcing that ‘One Rank, One Pension’ will be introduced by 2030, Tarique Rahman said welfare measures for both serving and retired members of the armed forces will be implemented gradually.

Praising the forces' contributions to the country, he said members of the armed forces have stood by people in remote hilly areas and during natural disasters, including floods and cyclones.

He also lauded the role of Bangladeshi peacekeepers, including female members, in the UN peacekeeping missions across the world.

Recalling that many members of the armed forces have been martyred or injured while serving the country in the Chattogram Hill Tracts and in UN missions, the Prime Minister prayed for the eternal peace of the martyrs' souls and expressed sympathy to their bereaved families and for those injured in the line of duty.

Expressing gratitude to the representatives of friendly countries for attending the reception, he recalled the contributions of their people during the Liberation War and appreciated their continued support in training and developing the armed forces.

Hoping that the cooperation would continue, he said Bangladesh, for its part, would remain committed to supporting global peacekeeping efforts under the United Nations.

Earlier in his speech, the Prime Minister became emotional while recalling his family's long association with Dhaka Cantonment, where his mother former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia had spent a major part of her life.

He said she had attended Armed Forces Day programmes both as prime minister and as leader of the opposition, and the 2025 reception was her last participation in the event.

Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and other members of the cabinet, members of parliament, the Chief Election Commissioner and election commissioners, leaders of different political parties, senior government officials, eminent persons, and ambassadors and high commissioners of different countries were present at the reception.

Descendants of Bir Sreshtho and other gallantry-awardee freedom fighters of the armed forces, members of the families of martyrs and injured people of the July-August mass uprising, and descendants of army members killed in the BDR carnage were also present on the occasion.

item.title: Chaos at Boishakhi TV office, DMD taken into police custody
item.description:
A dispute over an instruction for a journalist to resign triggered chaos at the office of private television channel Boishakhi TV on Saturday.

Employees of the channel alleged that outsiders entered the office and attempted to take away its Deputy Managing Director (DMD), Tipu Alam Milon.

The incident took place at the channel's office in Mohakhali, Dhaka, at around 3pm on Saturday.

A source at Boishakhi TV said police took DMD Tipu Alam into custody following the incident, which stemmed from an internal dispute. Police from Banani Police Station took him into custody.

Banani Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Salah Uddin told Prothom Alo, "We received information that unidentified outsiders had entered the office and were creating disorder. We went to the scene and later took the DMD into police custody for his security."

The OC said a case had been filed against DMD Tipu Alam Milon in connection with the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement.

Police were discussing whether to show him arrested in the case filed with Kotwali Police Station. Officers from that police station had arrived, he added.

What happened

During the incident, a person went live on the television channel's Facebook page, saying that a group of people had entered Boishakhi TV's premises and were carrying out attacks and vandalism.

Showing people gathered outside the building, the person said they had attacked and vandalised the newsroom.

An employee of the television channel, speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, said DMD Tipu Alam had asked HM Nahian, head of the online department, to resign at around 2pm.

Following the incident, Nahian brought leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal to the office, the employee alleged.
They then attempted to take the DMD away, triggering chaos and disorder involving the channel's employees. As more people gathered outside the main gate, the television channel's regular operations were disrupted.

Police from Banani Police Station subsequently arrived and brought the situation under control.

Asked about the incident, HM Nahian told Prothom Alo, "A disagreement developed between the DMD and me over the publication of a photo card. At one point, he asked me to resign. When I asked him to settle my salary dues, he told me to go to the human resources (HR) department.

"When I went there, the responsible official prepared the necessary documents. After returning from the DMD's room, the official informed me that outsiders were creating disorder."

item.title: 90 BGB platoons deployed in seven districts
item.description:
A total of 90 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed across seven districts to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and prevent possible incidents.
The deployment covers Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Mymensingh, Faridpur and Cox’s Bazar, according to the BGB media wing.
Of the deployed platoons, 18 are in Dhaka district, five in Dhaka metropolitan area, six in Narayanganj, 15 in Gazipur, 29 in Gopalganj, two in Mymensingh, five in Faridpur and six in Cox’s Bazar. Another four platoons remain on standby.
Acting on the directives of the Ministry of Home Affairs, BGB personnel will work in coordination with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies.
They will strengthen security and surveillance at key installations, industrial zones and other important locations, while working to prevent unrest, violence and activities that could threaten public safety.
BGB headquarters is also using technology-driven surveillance to monitor and coordinate operations on the ground. The system includes live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other modern equipment.

item.title: President, PM pay tribute to Armed Forces martyrs on Armed Forces Day
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday paid homage to the martyrs of the Bangladesh Armed Forces on the occasion of Armed Forces Day 2026.
The president, also the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, placed a wreath at Shikha Anirban in Dhaka Cantonment in the morning to pay tribute to the members of the Army, Navy and Air Force who made the supreme sacrifice during the 1971 Liberation War.
After laying the wreath, he stood in solemn silence for a while. A smartly turned-out contingent comprising members of the three services presented a salute, while a bugle played a mournful tune.
The president later signed the visitors' book at the memorial, according to a press release from his press wing.
The chiefs of the three services and senior officials of the Armed Forces Division received him upon his arrival.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also placed a wreath at Shikha Anirban in the morning and stood in solemn silence to honour the memory of the martyred armed forces members.
A contingent of the Army, Navy and Air Force presented a guard of honour, while the bugle played the Last Post. The Prime Minister, who is also in charge of the Ministry of Defence, later signed the visitors' book.
The three service chiefs received the prime minister at the memorial. He later visited the Armed Forces Division, where Chief of Army Staff General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan and Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Khandaker Mezb ul Azim paid him a courtesy call.
On the occasion, the service chiefs are also scheduled to pay a courtesy call on the president at Bangabhaban in the evening.
Various programs have been arranged across the country to mark the day and honour the members of the Armed Forces who sacrificed their lives during the Liberation War.
Special prayers will be offered at mosques in cantonments, naval bases and air force bases, seeking the welfare and prosperity of the country and the continued success of the Armed Forces.
The prime minister is also scheduled to exchange greetings with selected decorated freedom fighters and their successors at Dhaka Cantonment. A reception will be hosted at Senakunja in the cantonment at 4pm on his behalf.
On November 21, 1971, the Army, Navy and Air Force jointly launched a coordinated offensive against Pakistani occupation forces during the Liberation War. The day is observed every year as Armed Forces Day following the country's independence.

item.title: Chief justice: Judges must not use AI to write verdicts
item.description:
Judges may use artificial intelligence (AI) to search for relevant information and legal references, but must not rely on it to prepare or write verdicts, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury has said.
He stressed that the operative part of every verdict must be written personally by the concerned judge, based on their own judicial judgement, legal reasoning and analysis.
The chief justice made the remarks while addressing members of the Bangladesh Judicial Service working in courts and tribunals across Chittagong division at a program at Radisson Blu Bay View Hotel in Chittagong on Saturday.
Judicial officers from all 11 districts of the division — Chittagong, Comilla, Cox's Bazar, Noakhali, Brahmanbaria, Chandpur, Lakshmipur, Feni, Khagrachhari, Rangamati and Bandarban — attended the event.
He emphasised speeding up judicial proceedings, modernising case management, improving judicial efficiency and ensuring a court-friendly environment for litigants.
Highlighting the importance of social realities and a humane approach in judicial decisions, he said judges should consider the broader social context alongside the legal aspects of each case. He also called for a zero-tolerance approach to drug- and arms-related cases.
The chief justice stressed the need to create specialised judicial posts to make the justice system more effective. He said judges would be appointed to commercial courts once the necessary legal amendments were completed to establish and operationalise them.
He also said initiatives would be taken to arrange specialised training for judges in Bangladesh, with expert trainers from Japan, Australia and the United States.
On case and court management, he urged judges to prepare cause lists according to their capacity, announce the next hearing date in open court after hearings, ensure the security of case records and provide certified copies promptly.
He also called for adequate seating facilities for litigants in every district court and initiatives to establish daycare centres.
Addressing judicial conduct, he said a judge's behaviour outside the courtroom should also reflect the dignity, responsibility and character of the office. He urged judges to exercise caution and responsibility on social media, particularly Facebook, and refrain from using social media or carrying mobile phones while sitting in court.
The chief justice also urged lawyers to avoid unnecessarily lengthy arguments and keep hearing time limited and specific. Granting adjournments, he said, should not become a routine practice, as court time was valuable and must be used efficiently to expedite case disposal.
Several senior judicial officials, including Justice SM Kuddus Zaman, responsible for Chittagong-1, Justice Ahmed Sohel, responsible for Chittagong-2, and Supreme Court Registrar General Md Hemayet Uddin, also spoke at the program.
The chief justice called on all concerned to help ensure timely and effective justice, speed up case disposal, improve professional competence and strengthen public confidence in the judiciary.

item.title: Three Chittagong Board employees held over SSC result fraud
item.description:
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested three employees of the Chittagong Education Board, including a programmer, for their alleged involvement in manipulating SSC examination results.
The arrests came after investigators found evidence of their involvement in the fraud, the CID said.
Panchlaish Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mozammel Haque confirmed the arrests on Saturday.
The arrestees are Farhadul Islam, 29, an employee of the board's scanning section; Shahidul Alam Jisan, 27; and programmer Abdul Malek, 56. Farhadul is from Anwara upazila, Jisan from Halishahar in Chittagong city, and Malek from Gomostapur upazila in Chapainawabganj.
Mozammel Haque said a CID team from its Dhaka Crime Division, led by Police Inspector Russell, arrested the three during a raid on Wednesday night. They were later handed over to Panchlaish police.
CID investigation officer Inspector Russell said the three employees of the board's computer section, which handles result processing, were arrested after investigators found evidence of their involvement in the manipulation.
Some of them had been holding the same responsibilities for 13 years, he said, adding that the CID was investigating whether anyone else was involved.
The case was filed over allegations that the marks of a student who failed in 10 subjects in the 2026 SSC examinations were manipulated to secure a pass. Three employees of the board's computer section and the student were named in the case. The arrests were made as part of the investigation.

item.title: Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?
item.description:
The Taliban authorities in Afghanistan claim that the Pakistani government is supporting armed Afghan groups that are opposed to their rule, an accusation Islamabad denies.
Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi recently alleged that Pakistan had launched a “project to destabilize Afghanistan.”
He claimed that “thousands of armed individuals have gathered along the Durand Line [Afghanistan-Pakistan border] to undermine the stability achieved in Afghanistan.”
The accusations come after months of border clashes between Afghan Taliban and Pakistani forces.
In July, the Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF), an anti-Taliban group, reportedly clashed with Taliban forces in the Zebak district of Badakhshan, a northeastern Afghan province. The group said it also carried out attacks in Nooristan and Kunar provinces in October.
Another “resistance group,” the United Front of Afghanistan, claimed it attacked Taliban forces in Kandahar province along the border with Pakistan.
“The people who created insecurity in Badakhshan crossed from Chitral [in Pakistan] and later fled back to Chitral. They had been brought in. Even Pakistani military personnel were with them,” alleged Zabihullah Mujahid, the Taliban’s main spokesperson, in an interview with DW’s Pashto-Dari service in September.
Pakistan’s Ministry of Information swiftly dismissed the allegations as propaganda.
Groups that oppose Taliban rule in Afghanistan say they are not supported by any external force, and their resistance is purely indigenous.
More than five years since returning to power in Kabul, the Taliban have consolidated their control over Afghanistan and largely suppressed both armed resistance groups and political dissidents.
Shinkai Karokhail, a former Afghan lawmaker, told DW it would be logistically difficult for anti-Taliban Afghan groups to cross the Pakistani border and enter Afghanistan without Islamabad’s support, referring to clashes in Badakhshan and Nooristan provinces. “It is simply impossible,” she said.
The Taliban themselves maintained close ties with Pakistan in the 1990s during their first stint in power. Some US officials have even claimed that Islamabad didn’t relinquish its support to the Islamist group even after the 2001 September 11 terrorist attacks in the United States. Islamabad has always refuted these allegations.
Afrasiab Khattak, a Pakistani political analyst and former senator, believes that Pakistani support for anti-Taliban groups is “real.”
“Taliban opponents come to Islamabad, hold meetings, and it is a part of Pakistan’s policy toward Afghanistan,” he told DW.
Qandil Abbas, an associate professor of politics and international relations at Quaid-i-Azam University in Islamabad, disagrees.
“Pakistan may provide political support [to Taliban opponents], but not military support,” she told DW.
Ali Ahmad Jalali, a professor at the Near East South Asia Center for Strategic Studies at the National Defense University in Washington DC, said it is possible that Islamabad is backing opponents of the Taliban as “leverage.”
“When such incidents take place along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border, and given Pakistan’s history of support for Afghan groups, it would not be surprising if Pakistan is supporting these groups,” Jalali said.
Pakistani officials have repeatedly demanded that the Taliban take action against anti-Pakistan militant groups, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a militant group responsible for attacking Pakistani civilians and soldiers, and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), an outlawed armed separatist group active in its western Balochistan province.
Islamabad alleges that these groups organize and launch attacks on Pakistan from Afghan territory with Taliban support.
“Meaningful progress requires Afghan authorities to address legitimate security concerns of neighboring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism,” Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said this week at the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) summit in Islamabad.
The Pakistani government said on Friday that Afghanistan was not invited to participate in the ECO gathering as Pakistan does not recognize the Taliban regime in Kabul.
Jalali, who served as Afghanistan’s interior minister from 2003 to 2005, argued that Islamabad is demanding something the Taliban may neither be willing nor able to provide.
“Pakistan wants the Taliban to cooperate in fighting against groups such as the TTP. But the TTP has long fought alongside the Afghan Taliban. There are ideological as well as friendly ties between the two. They seek a similar political system, and some Afghan Taliban members may even be among TTP fighters,” the analyst added.
Experts also point to the Taliban’s efforts to strengthen relations with India, Pakistan’s long-standing regional rival, as a cause of concern for Islamabad.
Malek Sitez, an Afghan international relations researcher, argued that Pakistan was not keen on Kabul getting closer to New Delhi but added that Pakistan no longer had the kind of influence over Afghanistan that it had in the past.
Despite accusations and counteraccusations from both sides, Jalali did not believe that Pakistan was seeking regime change in Afghanistan.
“I do not think Pakistan can or wants to overthrow the Taliban and replace them with another group,” he underlined. Instead, he stressed, Islamabad’s objective is to pressure the Taliban into cooperating against the TTP.
Aziz Barez, a political analyst, was of the view that Afghan groups opposed to the Taliban could not fully trust Islamabad, adding that they may welcome alleged Pakistani support but are also aware that such backing could be temporary.
“It is possible that Pakistan and the Taliban will resolve their differences tomorrow and become close allies again,” he told DW.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s ‘special operation’
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a “special operation” by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighboring Yemen’s civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognized government against the Houthis.
An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was “under a hostile aerial threat.”
The coalition later said it had “intercepted and destroyed” three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.
The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition’s attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday.
The “special operation” hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.
It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities.
The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was “unsafe.” The group also threatened Riyadh’s financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had “targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles.”
The coalition also hit “military targets” in Sanaa, including missile and drone facilities and a supply depot, he said on X.
The Houthis said coalition strikes had killed 41 people in the previous 24 hours. Yemen’s Saudi-backed armed forces said dozens of airstrikes and drone attacks, as well as hundreds of artillery attacks, killed or wounded 193 Houthi fighters.
These figures were impossible to verify independently.
Two ballistic missiles were intercepted over the Jizan region near the Yemen border, the coalition spokesman said, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq.
The Houthi military spokesman said the group had targeted Al-Shuqaiq power station and Jizan port with “accurate and direct” strikes that caused “extensive damage.”
Images of a damaged power station in Mocha after a coalition air raid were broadcast by the Houthis’ Al-Masirah television.
The coalition strikes came after a Houthi attack struck a tower in Riyadh’s financial district, the latest high-profile blow against the world’s top oil exporter.
Witnesses told AFP that Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, housing Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, was damaged.
After the coalition warned civilians to evacuate Hodeida port, the Houthis responded by threatening to hit Jeddah and other ports on the Saudi Red Sea coast.
The Houthis’ Humanitarian Operations Coordination Centre sent emails to shipping companies and other bodies using Jeddah port, warning them to evacuate.
The group warned “all airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe, as it will be the theatre of our operations in the coming hours, except for the holy airspace over Mecca and Medina.”
They also told people to avoid Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District, whose offices were evacuated weeks ago, calling it a “military target.”
The two sides have exchanged attacks since a four-year truce in Yemen’s civil war collapsed in July.
Early on Friday, the Houthis accused the Saudis of striking a civilian boat, killing 19 people.
Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces withdrew from areas near the Red Sea’s Bab al-Mandab strait this month, ceding territory to the Houthis, who launched a sweeping offensive in September.
The group has now advanced close to Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognized government which fled the Houthis’ takeover of Sanaa in 2014.
The coalition intervened against the Houthis in early 2015, in a conflict that left hundreds of thousands dead and created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.
The United Nations expressed concern on Friday over the ongoing attacks.

item.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits central Peru
item.description:
A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities.
The earthquake occurred at 7:09pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers.
The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers.
Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.”
Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.”
AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake.
The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao.
Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.”
Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.”
Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire -- an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them.
A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes.

item.title: COP31 draft drops fossil fuel phase-out, gender pledges
item.description:
The latest revised draft of the COP31 cover decision has sparked fresh controversy after dropping explicit references to accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels and implementing the Belém Gender Action Plan, exposing deep divisions among countries over the summit's climate ambitions.
The revised text, circulated by the COP31 Presidency on Thursday afternoon, also removes references to persons with disabilities, narrows commitments on climate-related health impacts and leaves several critical issues unresolved as the summit approaches its scheduled conclusion on Friday.
While the draft retains a call to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035, it does not establish an agreed baseline for measuring the increase, raising questions about how the commitment will be implemented and monitored.
The developments have drawn criticism from climate advocates and vulnerable countries, who fear that political compromises are weakening accountability and undermining the interests of communities already experiencing the consequences of climate change.
Panama has emerged as one of the strongest critics of the revised language. Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro warned that his country would formally object at the closing plenary if the final outcome failed to meet its principles.
In a letter outlining Panama's demands, Navarro called for a cap on global oil production at current levels, immediate action on methane emissions, recognition of science as the foundation of climate policy and changes to the UN climate decision-making process to allow majority voting.
At a separate press conference, Navarro accused the petroleum industry of holding the world hostage.
"We are in love with our kidnappers," he said, describing governments' continued dependence on fossil fuel industries.
He also said 30 countries now supported efforts to develop a fossil fuel treaty outside the UN climate negotiations. Adaptation finance pledge faces questions over implementation
One of the central elements of the revised draft is its call to increase adaptation finance, but the absence of an agreed baseline has created uncertainty over the scale of the commitment.
The document estimates that developing countries will require approximately $305 billion annually for adaptation through 2035.
It asks the Standing Committee on Finance to present options for establishing a baseline in 2027 against which progress towards tripling adaptation finance can be measured.
A separate provision calls for efforts to at least triple annual outflows from specified multilateral climate funds by 2030, using 2022 as the baseline.
Teresa Anderson of ActionAid International said developing countries were being expected to undertake greater climate adaptation efforts without receiving adequate financial support.
"Adaptation is how we all survive this climate crisis together," she told journalists.
The proposed Antalya-to-Addis Ababa Roadmap on Adaptation and Resilience Finance is intended to identify predictable funding sources and improve countries' access to climate finance, including resources for addressing loss and damage.
The COP31 and COP32 presidencies would oversee the process and report on progress in 2027.
However, the roadmap does not specify new financial contributions from individual countries, leaving uncertainty over where the additional resources will come from.
The draft encourages greater use of grants and highly concessional public finance, particularly for least developed countries and small island developing states. It also calls on funding institutions to accelerate approvals, reduce transaction costs and simplify requirements for recipient countries.
The financing gap is particularly visible in the loss and damage mechanism.
According to the draft, funding requests submitted under the Barbados Implementation Modalities amount to approximately $2.8 billion, compared with allocations of only $342 million.
Of the $822 million pledged to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, only around half has been converted into actual contributions.
The draft also acknowledges that the Santiago Network and the Executive Committee of the Warsaw International Mechanism remain under-resourced.
Sandeep Chamling Rai, WWF's global climate change adaptation adviser, said communities already experiencing climate-related losses, including those in Nepal, urgently needed financial support.
He questioned whether the proposed roadmap would provide sufficient assurance that money would reach affected communities in time.
The funding shortfall remains a major concern for vulnerable countries, where climate-related disasters are increasing pressure on livelihoods, infrastructure and public services.
The removal of explicit fossil fuel language has become one of the most contentious aspects of the revised cover decision.
The earlier draft circulated on Monday had called for countries to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels, reflecting the commitment agreed at COP28 in Dubai.
However, Thursday's version no longer contains that explicit call.
Instead, it indirectly refers to the Dubai agreement by encouraging countries to reflect the outcomes of the first Global Stocktake in their national climate and adaptation plans.
Although the COP28 decision remains in force, campaigners fear that removing direct references from the COP31 outcome weakens political momentum towards implementing it.
The revised text also contains no reference to the just transition mechanism that countries agreed to develop at COP30 in Belém.
Negotiations on the mechanism are continuing separately under the Just Transition Work Programme.
Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is leading the COP31 negotiations, said countries were considering a two-part structure.
One component would provide political direction, while another would connect countries with technical experts, potential funders and existing initiatives to support the transition towards lower-emission economies.
However, the proposal does not include a commitment to establish a dedicated fund.
The revised draft proposes that electricity should account for 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035.
The target is linked to efforts to triple renewable energy capacity and double the global average annual rate of energy efficiency improvements by 2030.
However, the text does not establish a minimum share for clean electricity, meaning that additional power generated from coal and gas could also contribute towards the electrification target.
France's Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said her country would push for renewable energy and nuclear power to meet rising electricity demand.
Meanwhile, two proposals concerning carbon capture, utilisation and storage remain in brackets, indicating that countries have yet to reach agreement.
One proposal calls for capturing at least 500 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually by 2035, while working towards a longer-term range of 1.3 billion to 2.5 billion tonnes.
Another proposes working towards capturing 2.5 billion tonnes annually by 2035.
Vanuatu's Climate Minister Ralph Regenvanu questioned the prominence given to the technology, saying it had received more attention than it deserved.
The draft separately addresses carbon dioxide removal, stating that it should complement deep emissions reductions rather than replace them.
The revised text has also triggered concerns over the weakening of gender-related commitments and inclusive climate decision-making.
Four diplomats involved in the negotiations told journalists that Russia and the Vatican were seeking to block most references to gender in negotiating texts, while the European Union opposed those efforts.
The word "gender" does not appear anywhere in Thursday's cover draft.
Women are mentioned only once, in a paragraph listing relevant stakeholders.
The earlier draft had explicitly called for women and girls to participate fully in climate decision-making. The revised version also removes any specific role for women-led organisations in proposed annual workshops on access to climate finance between 2027 and 2030.
Although the Belém Gender Action Plan remains in force, campaigners are concerned that its implementation is receiving insufficient political attention.
The revised text also removes the explicit reference to persons with disabilities included in Monday's version.
While it encourages financial institutions to engage vulnerable communities, it does not explain how persons with disabilities will participate in funding decisions or how those processes will be made accessible.
Provisions recognising the importance of youth participation and Indigenous Peoples' leadership have, however, been retained.
The draft recognises intergenerational equity and calls for children and young people to have a meaningful voice in climate decisions. It also acknowledges the environmental stewardship and climate leadership of Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
The revised document has also narrowed its provisions on climate-related health impacts.
It recognises the growing consequences of climate change for physical and mental health and calls on governments to strengthen health systems by integrating health considerations into national adaptation plans.
However, it contains no dedicated commitment to health financing.
The earlier draft had specifically identified food and nutrition insecurity, damage to health facilities during extreme weather events and the importance of early warning systems for public health.
Those details have been removed from the revised health provision.
Notably, the words "food", "agriculture" and "nutrition" are absent from the document, while farmers are mentioned only once in the stakeholder list.
The text encourages locally led adaptation through sustainable land management, ecosystem restoration and measures to withstand drought, but does not assign farmers a specific role in deciding how adaptation finance should be allocated. Mountain communities and climate risks
The draft proposes establishing a Work Programme on Mountains and Climate Change under the Nairobi Work Programme.
The initiative would focus on improving climate observations, strengthening early warning systems and reducing disaster risks in mountain regions and glacier-dependent communities.
However, the programme would rely on existing funding channels rather than a dedicated financial mechanism.
The proposal also includes two technical dialogues and a high-level dialogue on mountains at COP32, although some details remain unresolved. 2.6°C warming projection highlights urgency
The draft acknowledges that full implementation of existing national climate plans would put the world on course for approximately 2.6°C of warming.
It also recognises that projected peak warming is likely to exceed the 1.5°C threshold and calls for any overshoot to be as small and brief as possible.
Fernanda de Carvalho, WWF's global head of climate and energy policy, welcomed the attention given to temperature overshoot, oceans and climate science.
However, she urged the COP31 Presidency to carry forward the COP30 roadmaps on fossil fuels and forests.
Outside the negotiating venue, climate activists staged a symbolic protest using missing-cat posters featuring a cat named Ambition to highlight what they described as the disappearance of climate ambition from the negotiations.
Philippine Menager of the Ecología y Desarrollo Foundation said campaigners wanted a clear roadmap for moving away from coal, oil and gas.
With the summit scheduled to conclude on Friday, negotiations remain intense. COP31 negotiation lead Chris Bowen said the Presidency would continue consultations with negotiating groups through Thursday night in an effort to secure consensus.
The final outcome will test whether countries can bridge their differences and deliver commitments that translate into meaningful action for vulnerable communities, or whether political disagreements will once again leave critical climate priorities unresolved.
This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organised by Internews' Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

item.title: All girls from class VI to X to receive stipends
item.description:
The government has decided to bring all girl students studying in classes VI to X, or equivalent levels, at general schools, colleges and madrasas under a universal stipend programme.
To implement the decision, the government has instructed students or their guardians to open bank, agent banking or mobile financial service accounts to receive the stipend payments directly.
Mohammad Asadul Haque, director of the Integrated Stipend Programme under the Prime Minister's Education Assistance Trust, issued the relevant directive on November 18.
Under the new arrangement, 100% of eligible girl students will receive stipends, while the existing system of financial assistance for male students will continue unchanged.
The payments will be made through the Government-to-Person (G2P) system. Students already registered in the programme's HSP-MIS software or receiving stipends will not need to open new accounts.
However, those not currently receiving stipends must open accounts in their own or their guardians' names.
The directive specifies that parents will normally serve as guardians. If neither parent is alive, siblings or grandparents may assume responsibility.
For mobile banking payments, the account and SIM must be registered using the designated parent's national identity card.
The directive also outlines procedures for students without eligible family guardians and requires educational institutions to monitor implementation.
Authorities concerned have been instructed to take urgent steps to ensure the programme's effective implementation.

item.title: কে হচ্ছেন জাতিসংঘের পরবর্তী মহাসচিব
item.description:
জাতিসংঘের পরবর্তী মহাসচিব কে হবেন, তা নিয়ে অচলাবস্থা এখনো কাটেনি। এ অচলাবস্থার মূলে সংস্থাটির স্থায়ী পাঁচ সদস্য। কোনো প্রার্থীর বিষয়েই তারা একমত হতে পারছে না।

ফলে গতকাল শুক্রবার জাতিসংঘের নিরাপত্তা পরিষদের নবম দফার অনানুষ্ঠানিক ভোটেও কোনো প্রার্থীকে চূড়ান্তভাবে বেছে নেওয়া সম্ভব হয়নি।

এখনো পর্যন্ত মহাসচিব পদে নির্বাচিত হওয়ার দৌড়ে এগিয়ে রয়েছেন কোস্টারিকার কূটনীতিক রেবেকা গ্রিনস্প্যান। শুক্রবার তিনি ১০টি ভোট পেয়েছেন, যা এই পদে নির্বাচিত হওয়ার জন্য যথেষ্ট। তবে নির্বাচিত হতে হলে নিরাপত্তা পরিষদের স্থায়ী পাঁচ সদস্য—যুক্তরাষ্ট্র, যুক্তরাজ্য, ফ্রান্স, রাশিয়া ও চীন—সবার সমর্থন পেতে হবে, কারও ভেটো বা আপত্তি থাকা চলবে না। এই পাঁচ দেশ থেকে দুটি ভোট গ্রিনস্প্যানের বিপক্ষে গেছে।

বর্তমান মহাসচিব আন্তোনিও গুতেরেসের উত্তরসূরি নির্বাচনের প্রক্রিয়ায় ১০০ দিনের বেশি সময় ধরে ভোট চলছে। এটি জাতিসংঘের ইতিহাসে সবচেয়ে দীর্ঘ সময় ধরে চলা মহাসচিব নির্বাচনপ্রক্রিয়া। গুতেরেসের দ্বিতীয় মেয়াদ আগামী ৩১ ডিসেম্বর শেষ হবে। নতুন মহাসচিব নির্বাচনে আগামী সপ্তাহে আবারও ভোট হওয়ার কথা রয়েছে।

বর্তমান মহাসচিব আন্তোনিও গুতেরেসের উত্তরসূরি নির্বাচনের প্রক্রিয়ায় ১০০ দিনের বেশি সময় ধরে ভোট চলছে। এটি জাতিসংঘের ইতিহাসে সবচেয়ে দীর্ঘ সময় ধরে চলা মহাসচিব নির্বাচনপ্রক্রিয়া। গুতেরেসের দ্বিতীয় মেয়াদ আগামী ৩১ ডিসেম্বর শেষ হবে। নতুন মহাসচিব নির্বাচনে আগামী সপ্তাহে আবারও ভোট হওয়ার কথা রয়েছে।

নিরাপত্তা পরিষদের যে দুই স্থায়ী সদস্য গ্রিনস্প্যানের বিরোধিতা করছে—ধারণা করা হচ্ছে, দেশ দুটি যুক্তরাষ্ট্র ও রাশিয়া। পরবর্তী ভোটের দিনে তাদের আপত্তি কাটিয়ে উঠতে পারলে গ্রিনস্প্যান হবেন জাতিসংঘের প্রথম নারী মহাসচিব।

সর্বশেষ ভোটে দ্বিতীয় অবস্থানে ছিলেন আর্জেন্টিনার রাফায়েল গ্রোসি। তিনি আটটি ‘সমর্থনসূচক’ ভোট পেয়েছেন। তবে নিরাপত্তা পরিষদের স্থায়ী পাঁচ সদস্যের মধ্যে তিনটি দেশ তাঁর বিরুদ্ধে ‘অসমর্থনসূচক’ ভোট দিয়েছে।

কিছুটা দেরিতে মহাসচিব পদের দৌড়ে নাম লেখান আরব আমিরাতের কূটনীতিক লানা নুসেইবেহ। তিনি সাতটি ‘সমর্থনসূচক’ ভোট পেয়েছেন। তবে নিরাপত্তা পরিষদের স্থায়ী পাঁচ সদস্যের মধ্যে তিনটি দেশ তাঁর বিপক্ষে ভোট দিয়েছে। এই বাধা পেরিয়ে তাঁর নির্বাচিত হওয়া কঠিন হতে পারে।

যদিও যুক্তরাষ্ট্র ও রাশিয়া প্রকাশ্যে তাঁর প্রতি সমর্থন জানিয়েছে। একাধিক সূত্রের তথ্য অনুযায়ী, ধারণা করা হচ্ছে, যুক্তরাজ্য, ফ্রান্স ও চীন কার্যত লানা নুসেইবেহর নির্বাচিত হওয়া আটকে দিয়েছে।

সুদানের ভয়াবহ সংঘাতের সঙ্গে সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের চলমান সংশ্লিষ্টতার কারণে লানা নুসেইবেহর প্রার্থিতা নিয়ে ব্যাপক সমালোচনা হয়েছে। যুক্তরাজ্যের পররাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী এড মিলিব্যান্ডকে লেখা এক চিঠিতে প্রায় ৭০ জন পার্লামেন্ট সদস্য যুক্তি দিয়েছেন, নুসেইবেহ ‘বিশ্বাসযোগ্য প্রার্থী’ নন। কারণ, সুদানে নৃশংসতার সঙ্গে আমিরাতের সংশ্লিষ্টতা নিয়ে জাতিসংঘের বিশেষজ্ঞ প্যানেলের প্রতিবেদনগুলো তিনি বারবার ‘অস্বীকার ও খারিজ’ করেছেন।

জাতিসংঘের বিশেষজ্ঞ প্যানেল ও মানবাধিকার সংগঠনগুলোর ধারাবাহিক প্রতিবেদন বলছে, সুদানের আধা সামরিক বাহিনী র‍্যাপিড সাপোর্ট ফোর্সেসকে (আরএসএফ) ভাড়াটে যোদ্ধা নিয়োগে সহায়তা এবং অস্ত্র সরবরাহ করেছে সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাত।

জাতিসংঘ ও যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী, এই বাহিনী দারফুরে গণহত্যা চালিয়েছে। সুদানে সংঘাতে জড়িত থাকার অভিযোগ অস্বীকার করেছে আমিরাত।
